canonical_title: Torwali English Dictionary for Students with pictures
license_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page; author uploaded own work

dialect_evidence.description: English abbreviations define black [چ] as Chail dialect and name the other dialect Sinkaen or Bahrain.
Urdu usage notes explain that [چ] marks the Chail realization in dialect-variant entries.

extraction.method: deterministic PDF glyph font/color/coordinate extraction; no OCR
extraction.seeded_sample_review_scope: IPA, gloss, POS, dialect marker, and inclusion status against rendered PDF pages; ToUnicode headword candidates are noncanonical

scope.included: IPA, POS, English definition, source-explicit Chail versus default Sinkaen/Bahrain dialect assignment, and explicit source relations on PDF pp. 14-230 (printed pp. 13-229); PDF ToUnicode headword candidates retained in the audit as locators
scope.excluded: Canonical Native values because the PDF ToUnicode map demonstrably corrupts some rendered Torwali headwords; front matter; illustrations; example sentences and scientific names from installed form fields (preserved in audit); source entries without IPA
scope.etymology_policy: No etymological links inferred; the dictionary makes lexical and variant/inflection claims only
scope.dialect_policy: The dictionary states that Torwali has Chail and Sinkaen/Bahrain dialects. Black [چ] marks Chail; unmarked records are assigned to the default Sinkaen/Bahrain variety. Source-specific dialect tags are deliberately distinct from SSNP survey tags.
